result.title: Neural expectation-maximization and meta-models
result.summary: We interpret Transformer networks as learned approximations to a hybrid probabilistic-inference procedure that combines max-product Loopy Belief Propagation (LBP) with Expectation--Maximization (EM). In this view, a Transformer performs inference in partially observed Markov Random Fields (MRFs) whose structure and parameters are not given a priori but are inferred from data. We show that self-attention implements a differentiable approximation to max-product LBP on an input-conditioned, dynamically structured MRF, with attention weights encoding learned structural affinities. We further establish an EM correspondence at the level of depth: each layer updates latent representations in an E-step-like forward pass, while the transition $θ^{(l)} \to θ^{(l+1)}$ across layers acts as an implicit M-step. Building on this interpretation, we introduce \emph{meta-models}, a design paradigm in which inputs generate instance-specific parameters, unifying mechanisms such as self-attention, mixture-of-experts, and gated units within a single framework. Empirical results support the proposed perspective.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将 Transformer 解释为 max-product LBP 与 EM 混合概率推断的学习近似：自注意力实现输入条件动态 MRF 上的可微 LBP，层级前向类似 E 步、层间参数转移类似隐式 M 步，并据此提出由输入生成实例特定参数的 meta-models 范式以统一注意力、MoE 与门控单元。
